Turn on the whitelist before an attack, not during one. Add your staff and regular players. Keep the list short and review it after the attack.

Test it: join from an account that is not on the list and confirm that it is refused. Then join from one that is on the list.

## Layer 3: maintenance mode

VeloFlame's maintenance mode can target a backend. Use it to stop new logins to one server while you restart it or clear a problem. Players already online stay where they are.

Use this during an attack on a single backend. Do not use it as the main defence.

## Layer 4: connection limits

FlameCord's documented controls include connection rate limits, account limits and latency thresholds. VeloFlame documents connection rate limiting. Set limits high enough for a real join spike. A server that loses a busy evening to strict limits loses players.

Start with the defaults. Watch the logs for a day. Then adjust one limit at a time.

## Layer 5: packet guards

Both products document packet-level protection. FlameCord has packet violation thresholds and kick rules. VeloFlame has packet guards. A client that breaks the protocol gets dropped before it can take more of the proxy's time.

Read the thresholds before you change them. A threshold that is too low kicks players on bad connections.

## Layer 6: logs

Check the logs after every change. You want to see:

- How many connections each limit rejected.
- Which IP ranges repeat.
- Whether any real player was refused.

If the logs show many refusals from one source, the firewall layer is the right place to block it.

## Compatibility notes

- VeloFlame's protocol constants cover 1.7.2 to 26.3. The repository's README is upstream Velocity text and names an artifact the build no longer emits. Use the release artifact from the product page, not the README, as your install reference.
- FlameCord's protocol table covers 1.8.x to 1.21.x and 26.x.
- Neither product's build Java version is a runtime requirement. Check the release notes before you deploy.

## What this guide does not cover

No setting makes a proxy immune to a large attack. These controls limit the damage and keep backends usable. For a large attack, add upstream protection at your hosting provider or network edge. That layer is outside these plugins.

For product details, see the [VeloFlame product page](/plugins/veloflame/) and the [FlameCord product page](/plugins/flamecord/).

## Frequently asked questions

### Does one setting stop a bot attack?

No. The guide uses a stack of controls, each catching what the layer above missed.

### Which proxy should I use on Velocity?

VeloFlame is the Velocity fork. Use FlameCord only on BungeeCord or Waterfall networks.

### Does this guide cover everything?

No. Read the section on what the guide does not cover.

---
# Reduce entity lag with mob and item stacking

URL: https://arkflame.com/guides/reduce-entity-lag-with-stacking/
Updated: 2026-11-07

Stack what repeats, then cap what keeps growing. MobStacker merges nearby mobs of the same type. FlameStack merges loose ground items and redstone-machine output. EntityLimiter sets hard caps on entity counts, and BlockLimiter caps blocks per chunk. Measure first, so you know which source costs the most.

## Measure before you stack

Read the [lag diagnosis guide](/guides/diagnose-lag-before-limiters/) first. It shows how to tell whether entities, redstone or blocks cause the cost. Change one source at a time. If you stack mobs and the lag was in redstone, you learn nothing from the change.

Record the tick and entity numbers before the change. Record them again after it. Without the before numbers, you cannot tell whether the change helped.

## What does MobStacker do?

MobStacker merges nearby mobs of the same type. Fewer entities means less tick cost from entity pressure. Two commands and a config file cover the stacking behaviour. The repository states no Minecraft version range, and its `api-version` 1.13 is the Bukkit API level, not a game-version claim.

Open the config on your server and set the behaviour you need before you go live. Test the stacking on a copy of a busy area first, so you can see how the stacks look to players.

## What does FlameStack do?

FlameStack stacks loose ground items and redstone-machine output. That covers the drops that pile up under farms. It is built against the Bukkit, Spigot and Paper API 1.13+, and it detects Folia at runtime. The [redstone guide](/guides/redstone-lag-without-breaking-farms/) walks through stacking ground items around a farm without breaking the farm.

FlameStack and MobStacker cover different entities. Use both if your server has both problems. Do not expect either one to fix the other's source.

## When do you need a hard cap?

Stacking lowers counts. It does not stop growth. EntityLimiter sets hard caps on entity counts to prevent crash and lag from entity pressure. It ships eight configuration files for limits, messages and behaviour. Use it after stacking, so the caps catch only what stacking misses.

## What about blocks?

Dense player builds cost load and save time. BlockLimiter caps block counts per chunk. Limits are set per block type, so you can cap the blocks your players build most without touching the rest. The plugin's descriptor is at version 1.0.9.

## What about redstone?

Redstone machines are a separate cost. RedstoneLimiter watches activations at block, sub-chunk, chunk and 32×32-chunk region scope. It cancels or throttles work that crosses the configured limits. It also has a monitor-only mode. Run it in monitor mode first, then enforce limits once you know which machines cross the line.

## Order of work

1. Measure with the lag guide.
2. Stack mobs with MobStacker and ground items with FlameStack.
3. Cap entity counts with EntityLimiter.
4. Cap blocks per chunk with BlockLimiter.
5. Run RedstoneLimiter in monitor mode, then enforce.

Stop after each step and measure again. If the numbers stop improving, the next source is probably not the one you assumed.

## How to tell the stacking worked

Compare the same measurements before and after. Look at the entity count in the area you stacked, then at tick time under the load that caused the problem. A drop in entity count with no change in tick time means the entities were not the cost. Go back to the lag guide and measure the next source.

Also check player reports. Stacked mobs or items can look different. If players cannot find their loot or cannot see a mob they want to fight, adjust the stacking config before you add the next plugin.

## What about Folia?

FlameStack detects Folia at runtime. EntityLimiter and BlockLimiter declare Folia support in their repositories. RedstoneLimiter also declares it. Check each one on your own build. The [Folia compatibility guide](/guides/folia-compatibility/) explains what the flag does and does not prove.

## Frequently asked questions

### Does stacking replace limits?

No. Stacking merges what exists. EntityLimiter caps what keeps growing.

### Is FlameStack the same as MobStacker?

No. FlameStack stacks ground items and redstone-machine output. MobStacker stacks mobs.

### Does EntityLimiter work on Folia?

The repository declares Folia support. Verify it on your own build before you rely on it.

### Which plugin should I install first?

Measure first. The lag guide shows how to find which source costs the most, then install the matching plugin.

---
# Reduce redstone lag without breaking farms

URL: https://arkflame.com/guides/redstone-lag-without-breaking-farms/
Updated: 2026-11-07

Redstone lag and farm breakage have the same root cause: a limit that is too broad. A cap that stops a lag machine also stops a working farm. The fix is to measure first, cap the machines that cost the most, and leave the rest alone.

This guide uses three plugins. RedstoneLimiter controls redstone activations. FlameStack merges ground items and machine output so they take up fewer entity slots. EntityLimiter caps entity counts. Use only the ones your lag report points to.

## Step 1: measure in monitor mode

RedstoneLimiter has a monitor mode. It observes activations without cancelling anything. Turn it on, let a normal play period run, and read its statistics.

Look for the scopes where activations concentrate. RedstoneLimiter tracks activations at block, sub-chunk, chunk and region scope. A hot spot at chunk scope is a different problem from one at block scope. Note the world and the area.

Do not enforce anything until you have a list of the machines causing the load.

## Step 2: check entities separately

Redstone is not always the cause. Mob farms and item drops can cost as much as a redstone clock. Check entity counts before you cap redstone.

EntityLimiter caps entity counts. Its shipped defaults use a radius mode with a radius of 16. The default cap is 32 per area, with per-type caps such as 16 for zombies and 40 for horses. Those are defaults. Adjust them to your server's layout and mob farms.

Run EntityLimiter in its own test window so you can tell which change did what.

## Step 3: stack ground items

Ground items and machine output build up around farms. FlameStack merges loose ground items and redstone-machine output into stacks. That reduces entity pressure without removing any items.

Test it on a copy of a farm first. Check that the output still reaches the collection point and that the stacked items still count correctly in the chest or hopper that receives them.

## Step 4: cap the machines, not the redstone

Once you know the hot spots, use RedstoneLimiter's overrides. It supports presets, per-world overrides and per-material overrides.

- Use a per-world override for a world that is only for testing or building.
- Use a per-material override for the machine that is causing the load.
- Leave the default limits alone for everything else.

Do not set a broad limit on all redstone to fix one machine. That is how working farms break.

## Step 5: check the farms

After each change, run the farm for a full cycle and count the output. Compare it with the same cycle before the change.

If output drops, widen the override for that material, or move the limit to a different scope. Do not remove the limit without checking what caused the drop.

## Step 6: watch the notifications

RedstoneLimiter has an in-game GUI, statistics and notifications. Use the notifications during the first few days. They show which machines hit a limit, which tells you whether a limit is hitting a farm that should be left alone.

## Folia

RedstoneLimiter declares Folia support, and its tutorial documents Folia scheduling. A declaration is not a test. Run the setup on a Folia test server before you change production. For the scheduling rules, read the [Folia compatibility guide](/guides/folia-compatibility/).

## Common mistakes

- Enforcing before measuring. You cannot tell which limit fixed the lag.
- Using one global limit. It breaks farms that were working.
- Changing redstone and entity limits in one step. You lose the ability to tell which one helped.
- Skipping the output check. A farm that runs at half speed looks fine in the logs.

For the product details, see the [RedstoneLimiter product page](/plugins/redstonelimiter/), the [FlameStack product page](/plugins/flamestack/) and the [EntityLimiter product page](/plugins/entitylimiter/).

For a wider method, see [diagnose lag before limiters](/guides/diagnose-lag-before-limiters/).

## Frequently asked questions

### Why do farms break when I fix redstone lag?

A limit that is too broad stops working farms along with the lag machine. Cap the machines that cost the most.

### Which plugins does this guide use?

RedstoneLimiter, FlameStack and EntityLimiter. Use only the ones your lag report points to.

### Where should I start?

Measure in monitor mode first, then cap the machines that cost the most.

---
# Set up Discord role and chat sync with DiscordFlow

URL: https://arkflame.com/guides/discord-role-and-chat-sync-setup/
Updated: 2026-11-07

DiscordFlow connects a Minecraft network to Discord. It syncs roles, syncs chat, adds proximity voice and lets staff run console commands from Discord. It runs on Bukkit-family servers with a BungeeCord or Velocity bridge. Plan the proxy part first, then add the backend modules, then test each sync with a test account.

## What DiscordFlow covers

The plugin has four feature areas: Discord role sync, Discord chat sync, proximity voice integration and console access from Discord. It ships Bukkit, BungeeCord and Velocity modules. The repository states support for 1.8 through 1.21+ and requires Java 11 or newer. JDA is bundled in the universal artifact, so you do not install it separately.

Because the proxy and backend need different modules, decide the topology before you install anything. The [DiscordSRV alternative guide](/guides/discordsrv-alternative-discordflow/) compares the plugin with the older option and covers when each one fits.

## Choose the topology

A single Spigot or Paper server needs the Bukkit-family module only. A network with a proxy needs the BungeeCord or Velocity module on the proxy, and the Bukkit-family module on each backend that players reach. Install the module that matches each jar. Do not put the proxy module on a backend.

## Set up the bot first

Create the Discord bot and invite it to your server before you touch the Minecraft config. Give it only the permissions it needs for role management and the channels you plan to sync. Check the bot's role position. A bot below the roles it manages cannot change them.

## Configure role sync

Map each Discord role to the Minecraft group or permission that goes with it. Start with one role, such as a verified-member role, and test it with a test account. Confirm the role appears in Discord and the permission applies in game. Add the staff roles last, after the basic mapping works.

## Configure chat sync

Pick one channel for each direction you want. Two-way sync on a busy channel doubles the message flow, so start with one channel. Test with a short message, a long message and a message with formatting, since each one can break differently. Keep the ChatSentinel filter on the Minecraft side if you already use it, so spam does not reach Discord.

## Set up proximity voice

Proximity voice is one of the four feature areas, so test it separately from role and chat sync. Test it with two accounts standing at different distances. Check the voice settings in the config before you invite players, and change one value at a time.

## Enable console access carefully

Console access lets staff run commands from Discord. It is powerful. Restrict it to the staff roles that need it, and log every command. Do not give it to a general role. Test with a harmless command, such as a broadcast, before you use a command that changes player data.

## Test order

1. Install the proxy module on the proxy and the Bukkit-family module on each backend.
2. Start the network and confirm each module loads without errors.
3. Map one role and test it with a test account.
4. Enable one chat channel and send test messages in both directions.
5. Configure proximity voice and test two accounts at different distances.
6. Restrict console access to staff, then test one harmless command.

## Common failure points

If a player has the Discord role but not the in-game permission, check the role mapping first. A bot below the managed roles cannot change them, so check the bot's role position. Read the console on every server in the network, since each module logs on its own server.

## What this does not do

DiscordFlow syncs roles and chat. It does not punish players. For mutes, bans and warnings, use a punishment plugin such as [SMP Punishments](/plugins/smp-punishments/). For staff tools inside the game, [StaffModeX](/plugins/staffmodex/) provides staff-mode inventories and moderation tools.

## Frequently asked questions

### Does DiscordFlow need a proxy?

Not for a single server. A network with a proxy needs the BungeeCord or Velocity module on the proxy.

### Does the universal artifact include JDA?

Yes. The repository states that JDA is bundled in the universal artifact.

### Which Java version does it need?

The repository requires Java 11 or newer.

### Does DiscordFlow punish players?

No. It syncs roles, chat, voice and console access. Use a punishment plugin for mutes and bans.

---
# SMP moderation setup: punishments, staff mode and chat

URL: https://arkflame.com/guides/smp-moderation-and-punishments-setup/
Updated: 2026-11-07

Set moderation up in layers. Punishments come first, then staff tools, then chat filters, then anticheat alerts. SMP Punishments covers bans, kicks, mutes and warnings. StaffModeX gives staff their inventories and tools. ChatSentinel filters chat. Each layer needs its own permissions, and each one needs a test before players see it.

## Start with SMP Punishments

SMP Punishments covers bans, kicks, mutes and warnings. It has an optional voice-chat mute hook. The suite has twenty-five commands and thirty-eight permissions. Give staff the permissions by rank, not by name, so you can change a rank without editing each player.

Test each command with a test account before you give staff access. Check that a warning is recorded, a mute blocks chat, and a ban stops a login. A punishment that does not do what the command says is the most damaging bug a moderation plugin can have.

## Add staff mode

StaffModeX provides staff-mode inventories, moderation tools and optional BungeeCord or Velocity modules. Its commands, permissions and configuration are documented in the repository. Install the proxy module only on a network that uses a proxy. On a single server, the Bukkit module is enough.

Keep staff mode separate from player permissions. Test entering and leaving staff mode with a test account before you give it to staff.

## Filter chat

ChatSentinel filters messages. It runs regex rules on Bukkit, BungeeCord and Velocity. It does not punish anyone, so pair it with SMP Punishments. Set the `punishments` section to the console commands your punishment plugin runs. The [chat spam guide](/guides/stop-chat-spam-and-advertising/) covers the blacklists and alert setup in order.

Check the alert channel before you launch. An offense that produces no alert is an offense staff never see.

## Add anticheat alerts

[FairPlay](/plugins/fairplay/) is the combat anticheat. It has permission-scoped alerts, punishments and ban waves. Keep it in alert mode for the first week, and point its alerts at staff who review them. Turn on punishments only after the alerts match what you saw in play.

## Order of work

1. Install SMP Punishments and test every command with a test account.
2. Set the staff ranks and permissions.
3. Install StaffModeX and test staff-mode entry and exit.
4. Configure ChatSentinel with punishment commands and an alert channel.
5. Install FairPlay in alert mode.
6. Review alerts for a week before you enable punishments.

## Who should see what

Give each rank only the moderation commands it needs. Junior staff need warnings and mutes. Senior staff need bans. Use the permission system to split them, and test each split with a test account on each rank.

Decide where staff look up past punishments before you launch. Test the lookup with a punishment issued from a second staff account, so you know the record is readable by the people who need it.

## Test the whole chain

Run one full scenario with a test account. Post an advertisement in chat, get the offense recorded, get the mute applied and check that staff saw the alert. A chain that works only in parts is not ready.

## Common mistakes

Do not enable punishments before you test them. Do not give every staff member the ban command on day one. Do not set chat filters so strict that normal conversation fails. Each of these is easy to avoid and hard to undo after players react.

## Folia

SMP Punishments declares Folia support in its repository. StaffModeX also declares it. ChatSentinel's Bukkit module declares the Folia flag as an API-level claim. Verify each one on your Folia build. The [Folia compatibility guide](/guides/folia-compatibility/) explains what each flag covers.

## Frequently asked questions

### Does ChatSentinel ban players?

No. It runs the console commands you list under `punishments`. Use SMP Punishments or another punishment plugin for bans and mutes.

### Do I need the proxy module for StaffModeX?

Only if your network uses a BungeeCord or Velocity proxy and you want proxy awareness.

### Should FairPlay punish players on day one?

No. Run it in alert mode for about a week, then turn on punishments.

### How do I test a punishment safely?

Use a test account. Confirm that a mute blocks chat and a ban stops a login, then remove the punishment and confirm the account is back to normal.

---
# Stop chat spam and advertising on a Minecraft server

URL: https://arkflame.com/guides/stop-chat-spam-and-advertising/
Updated: 2026-11-07

Run a chat filter with folder-based blacklists, flood and similarity checks, and alerts to staff. ChatSentinel does this. It applies regex rules to chat and runs on Bukkit, BungeeCord and Velocity. It filters messages, but it does not punish anyone. You still need a mute or ban setup for repeat offenders.

## What does ChatSentinel check?

The bundled modules cover folder-based blacklists (`security`, `advertisement`, `offense`, `user` and `client`), capitalization, flood, similarity, cooldown, syntax, allowed characters, correction, server mute and a join-location movement gate. The `advertisement` folder holds the blacklist for ad text. Put your server's domain and the ad patterns you see most often there.

The plugin also ships whitelist rule sets and message configuration. The repository lists fourteen permissions. Check them before you give staff access to the alert and reload commands.

## Where does it filter?

Chat comes first. The module set also covers private messages, signs, books, anvil renames and commands. That matters because spam often moves to a private message once the public chat is filtered.

## Who punishes the offender?

ChatSentinel does not. Offense responses are a list of console commands under `punishments`. The config recommends LiteBans or AdvancedBans for mutes. Write those commands before you go live, then test them with a test account.

## How do staff see what was blocked?

Alerts go to a Discord webhook and, optionally, Redis. Chat clear prints blank lines, controlled by `chat-snapshot.clear-lines`, which defaults to 128. The repository states that message history is no longer stored. If you need a record of blocked messages, the Discord webhook is the place to keep it.

## Which platforms does it run on?

ChatSentinel uses one shared checking core with entry points for Bukkit and Spigot, BungeeCord and Velocity. The Bukkit module declares `api-version: "1.13"` and `folia-supported: true`. Those are API levels, not a game-version promise. The repository states no Minecraft version range.

## When does ChatSentinel Premium help?

ChatSentinel Premium is a tuned smart chat-filter configuration for spam and swearing. It is sold separately and requires the ChatSentinel plugin. Use it when you want a ready configuration rather than writing the rules yourself. The base plugin is the right start if you want to control every list.

## Which rules should you tune first?

Start with advertising and flood. Those two cause the most damage in a public chat. Add swearing filters after you have read a few days of alerts. Changing many rules at once makes it hard to see which one caught a legitimate message.

Check similarity and cooldown on a busy channel. A strict cooldown can stop normal conversation during an event. Test that case before you enable the rule for everyone.

## Steps

1. Install ChatSentinel on the proxy or server that handles chat: Bukkit or Spigot, BungeeCord, or Velocity.
2. Edit the `advertisement` blacklist for your domain and common ad patterns.
3. Set `punishments` to the console commands your mute or ban plugin runs.
4. Connect a Discord webhook for alerts.
5. Test with a test account. Post a link, repeat a message quickly, and check that the alert arrives.

## Tune flood and similarity checks

Flood and similarity checks catch repeated messages. Both can catch ordinary players too. A player who types the same word in quick succession during a game is a common false positive. Set the cooldown first. Read the alerts for a day, then change the similarity threshold only if the alerts show a real pattern.

Keep the capitalization and syntax checks lighter than the ad blacklist. Capitals and punctuation annoy players, but they seldom carry an ad. Strict rules on those checks cost more goodwill than they save.

## Keep a record of blocked messages

The repository states that message history is no longer stored. Your Discord webhook is the record. If staff need a history of blocked messages for a dispute, decide where that record lives before the first offense. Set the webhook channel to one that staff can search, and keep its retention in line with your own rules.

## Frequently asked questions

### Does ChatSentinel ban players?

No. Offense responses run the console commands you list under `punishments`.

### Does ChatSentinel store chat history?

No. The repository states that message history is no longer stored.

### Does it work on Velocity?

Yes. ChatSentinel has a Velocity entry point, alongside the Bukkit, Spigot and BungeeCord entry points.

### Do I need Redis?

No. Redis alerts are optional. Discord webhooks are the main alert path.

---
# Tune ExploitFixer packet limits from /ef logs

URL: https://arkflame.com/guides/exploitfixer-packet-abuse/
Updated: 2026-10-30

An ExploitFixer alert means one module fired for one player at one VLS. It does not mean the global packet size limit is too low. Read the log first, find the module, and keep `cancel-packets` at its shipped default until you can test the exact client behavior on a staging server. The [ExploitFixer product page](/plugins/exploitfixer/) lists the modules. This guide covers how to read them.

## Confirm HamsterAPI before touching config

HamsterAPI is a hard runtime requirement. The descriptor lists it under `softdepend`, but startup aborts with `HamsterAPI is missing or disabled. ExploitFixer cannot start.` and logs a severe warning if the installed version is below `0.3.5`. PacketEvents and ProtocolLib are optional decoded-packet adapters, set by `PacketHooks.packet-events` and `PacketHooks.protocol-lib`.

If the plugin isn't running, no packet limit matters yet. Fix the dependency, then go back to the logs. The install and startup steps are in the [ExploitFixer docs](/docs/exploitfixer/).

## Read the evidence before opening YAML

- `/ef logs recent [page]` prints player, module, VLS, date and reason for recent alerts.
- `/ef logs most [page]` ranks players by alert count. Use it to find a repeat offender, not a noisy module.
- `/ef notifications` toggles your own alerts. Players only.
- `/ef checks` lists modules and their state. `/ef checks disable <module>` isolates one module while you reproduce the alert.
- `/ef checks` needs `exploitfixer.admin`, and `/ef logs` needs `exploitfixer.logs`. The code checks both, but neither is in `plugin.yml`. Grant them to staff explicitly. Don't assume op-like behavior.

Module toggles live in memory only. `EFModule.setEnabled` flips a field and doesn't write YAML, so a restart restores the configured value. Re-enable the module when the test ends.

## Know which file owns the number

| Setting | File | Shipped default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Violations.cancel` | `config.yml` | `25` VLS |
| `Violations.reduce` | `config.yml` | `20` VLS per second |
| `packet-limiter.max_size` | `modules/packet-limiter.yml` | `50kb` |
| `packet-limiter.tab_complete_limit` | `modules/packet-limiter.yml` | `256` |
| `packet-limiter.max_pps` / `max_bps` | `modules/packet-limiter.yml` | `4096` / `60kb` |
| `packet-watchdog.vls` | `modules/packet-watchdog.yml` | `25.0` per logical packet |
| `packet-watchdog.source-window-ms` | `modules/packet-watchdog.yml` | `5000` |
| `packet-watchdog.duplicate-leniency` | `modules/packet-watchdog.yml` | 3 failures in 2000 ms |
| `packet-watchdog.budgets.packet` | `modules/packet-watchdog.yml` | `1000` ms |

The shipped `Violations` block has its own warning: don't change those numbers, and don't remove `kick`, `cancel` or `notify`. At 100 VLS, the default command list already includes `kick` and a one-minute tempban. That escalation is why a small threshold change can cause a ban wave. Tune module budgets before you touch global escalation.

## Why cancel-packets stays false

`cancel-packets` defaults to `false` for a documented reason. Cancelling movement packets such as Pos and PosRot drops them from the HamsterAPI pipeline, which looks like an instant disconnect. Turning it on turns an alert into a failure the client can see.

PacketWatchdog also enforces a hard minimum of 100 VLS for punitive commands, whatever the global `Violations.commands` table says. The notify command works at any threshold. Don't use this as a way to quiet alerts.

## A tuning order that does not guess

1. Collect a normal play sample, not an attack sample. Use `/ef logs most` to see whether one player dominates, and `/ef logs recent` for the module and reason.
2. If the reason is one item, one book or one tab request, change the narrow key first: `item_limits.lore` (`96`), `book_limits.pages` (`50`), or `tab_complete_limit` (`256`).
3. Disable only the suspect module with `/ef checks disable <module>`, reproduce, then re-enable it. If the alerts stop, you've found the owner.
4. Change one value, run `/ef reload`, and check the same log view. `/ef reload` needs `exploitfixer.admin`.
5. Raise `max_size` last, and only for legitimate traffic that keeps exceeding it. Hex-colored item names are a documented false-positive source.
6. Keep `Debug.enabled` off in production. Turn it on briefly when the reason string doesn't name a packet type, then turn it off.

## Frequently asked questions

### Should I raise the global packet limit when one alert fires?

No. An alert means one module fired for one player. Read the log to find that module first.

### Does ExploitFixer need HamsterAPI?

Yes. HamsterAPI is a hard runtime requirement. Startup aborts without it.

### Should I change cancel-packets?

Keep it at the shipped default until you can test the exact client behavior.

---
# What folia-supported: true proves, and how to verify

URL: https://arkflame.com/guides/folia-compatibility/
Updated: 2026-10-30

`folia-supported: true` in `plugin.yml` says the author intends the plugin to run on Folia. It is not proof that it works. Folia replaces the single main-thread tick loop with region-owned scheduling. What matters is whether every world, block and entity access happens on the thread that owns that state.

## What the flag does and doesn't do

Folia reads the flag at load time. A true value means the plugin claims support. Folia doesn't inspect the code that runs afterward. A plugin can pass the load check and still call `Bukkit.getScheduler()` or touch a block in another region.

Treat the flag as the start of a checklist. It doesn't prove:

- that tasks are scheduled on the correct region.
- that cross-region teleports, block edits or entity lookups are safe.
- that third-party hooks or optional dependencies are Folia-aware.
- that reload and shutdown paths are clean.
- a Minecraft or Java runtime range.

## The scheduling model in practice

Folia has global, region, async and entity-scoped work. The names differ by API version, but the ownership rule holds. Global work goes to the global scheduler. Work tied to a location goes to the region scheduler of the region that owns that location. Background work goes async. Entity changes go through that entity's scheduler. Code that assumes one main thread will eventually throw, often as `UnsupportedOperationException`.

Real adapters in these repositories show the pattern:

- **RedstoneLimiter** wraps a `FoliaAPI` adapter. Player and entity work goes through `runTaskForEntity(...)`, region work through `runTaskForRegion(World, chunkX, chunkZ, ...)`, global work through `FoliaAPI.runTask`, and background maintenance on the async scheduler when it's available.
- **EntityLimiter** uses `FoliaAPI.runTaskTimerAsyncCancellable` for its tracker and `FoliaAPI.runTask(chunk, ...)` for chunk-scoped work.
- **BlockLimiter** branches on `FoliaAPI.isFolia()` and uses `FoliaAPI.runTaskForEntity(player, ...)` for player-scoped refresh work.
- **MobStacker** notes that async coordinator tasks stay async while entity work is handed to the entity scheduler. Its merge task has a separate `isFolia()` branch.

These are code-level adaptations, not proof that every path in each plugin is covered. They're still stronger evidence than a descriptor flag.

## "Region" means two different things

RedstoneLimiter calls a 32x32-chunk area a region in its stats and config. That's not a Folia scheduler region. If you tune a RedstoneLimiter scope while chasing a Folia scheduling error, you're mixing two vocabularies and will look in the wrong place.

SMP-Regions documents its Folia model: global work on the global scheduler, location work on the region scheduler, background scanning and file queuing on the async scheduler, no raw threads and no fake async completions. Ask for that level of detail from any plugin that claims Folia support.

## A verification checklist

1. Confirm the descriptor has `folia-supported: true` and note its `api-version`. The API level is a Bukkit API level, not a game-version guarantee.
2. Start the server and read the first thirty seconds of console. AuthMePremium, for example, should log `FoliaAPI initialized`. A missing adapter line is a warning sign.
3. Join with two accounts in different regions and trigger the feature in both. Region bugs often appear only when two owners are active.
4. Exercise entity work: spawn, remove, teleport and damage an entity. Watch for wrong-thread or ownership exceptions.
5. Exercise block work at a chunk boundary, then at a region boundary. Place and break the block from a player on each side.
6. Run the plugin's reload command, then repeat steps 3 to 5. Reload paths are where stale schedulers hide.
7. Search the log for `UnsupportedOperationException`, `not supported`, `wrong thread` and the plugin's own scheduler messages. A clean startup doesn't mean a clean test.

For a large plugin, repeat the checklist on a staging server with the same optional dependencies you run in production.

## When it fails

AuthMePremium's operational docs give the fix pattern for a Folia `UnsupportedOperationException`. Confirm the descriptor flag, confirm the backend runs the current universal JAR, confirm `FoliaAPI initialized` appears, and route player changes through the entity scheduler. Don't swap the failing call for a raw Bukkit scheduler call. That moves the error instead of fixing ownership.

If a third-party plugin throws, capture the full stack trace before disabling anything. The class and method in the trace usually name the owner faster than a plugin list.

## Frequently asked questions

### Does the folia-supported flag prove the plugin works on Folia?

No. It declares intent. Test region ownership on your own build.

### Does Folia check the code that runs after load?

No. Folia reads the flag at load time. It does not inspect the code that runs afterward.

### Can a plugin pass the load check and still fail?

Yes. The guide gives an example of a plugin that calls the global scheduler or touches a block in another region after loading.

---
# AuthMe Premium install and topology

URL: https://arkflame.com/docs/authme-premium/
Updated: 2026-10-30

## What it does

AuthMe Premium bridges premium, cracked, and Bedrock login state between a Bungee-compatible or Velocity proxy and Bukkit/Paper/Folia backends. It works with AuthMe Reloaded, Vault groups, Floodgate/Geyser detection, YAML/MySQL/MEMORY profiles, and proxy plugin messages.

It does not replace the proxy, AuthMe, Geyser, Floodgate, the firewall, or forwarding security. Premium proof comes from proxy online-mode verification. A username lookup is never proof. Bedrock auto-login needs a verified Floodgate path or the configured backend fallback.

## The two modes

The repository documents exactly two session bridge modes, both proxy-side.

**Mode A (default)** uses the proprietary `authmp:*` plugin-message bridge. Every backend that receives proxy players needs the AuthMePremium Bukkit companion. The companion handles AuthMe 5.x auto-login, Bedrock completion, Vault group changes, and `SYNC_CRACKED_STATE`.

**Mode B (optional)** sets `bridge.authme-native.enabled: true`. It is Velocity-only. Standard AuthMeReloaded 6.0.0+ backends read the native `authme:main` channel, so session continuity does not need the Bukkit companion. Bungee-compatible proxies, AuthMe 5.x backends, Bedrock completion, Vault group changes, and `SYNC_CRACKED_STATE` still require Mode A.

Mode B backends need AuthMeReloaded 6.0.0+, `Hooks.bungeecord: true`, and a `Hooks.proxySharedSecret` that matches the proxy's `bridge.authme-native.shared-secret`. In proxy or network deployments, disable AuthMe DataSource caching and keep clocks in sync. AuthMe rejects stale signed messages.

## Requirements

- One supported proxy (Bungee-compatible or Velocity). The universal JAR carries both proxy and Bukkit entrypoints.
- JDK 21 to build. `common`, `bukkit`, and `bungee` compile for Java 17; `velocity` compiles for Java 21. The install doc says to run Bukkit on Java 17+.
- AuthMe Reloaded on each backend where AuthMe login or register state must change.
- Mode A: the same JAR on the proxy and every backend that receives proxy players.
- Mode B: AuthMe 6.0.0+ backends and the shared secret above.

The Bukkit descriptor declares `api-version: "1.20"` and `folia-supported: true`. These are declarations, not a verified matrix.

## Install

1. Build with Maven: `mvn clean test`, then `mvn clean package`.
2. Use the universal artifact. `universal/pom.xml` sets `finalName` to `authmepremium-${project.version}`, currently `authmepremium-2.7.2.jar`. The README's `2.2.1-SNAPSHOT` is stale.
3. Mode A: put that JAR on the proxy and every backend behind it.
4. Approve each backend's proxy UUID with `/authmepremium pendingproxies` and `/authmepremium approveproxy <uuid>`. An empty allow-list only auto-approves the first UUID.
5. Keep backend ports private to trusted proxy addresses.
6. Mode B: enable `bridge.authme-native.enabled`, match the shared secret, and list `login-source-servers` and `target-servers`.

## Configure

Proxy `proxy-config.yml` defaults include:

```yaml
provider: YAML
database:
  type: YAML
protection:
  block-commands-unauthenticated: true
auto-premium: true
self-service-commands:
  require-permission: false
```

Backend `bukkit-config.yml` enables the AuthMe hook, keeps Vault off, and sets the auto-login timeout to `15` seconds with `5` retries. `bridge.plugin-message.token` ships empty. Set one explicit shared token; do not rely on learning it.

## Commands

Proxy admin commands require `authmepremium.usage`:

- `/authmepremium setpremium <player> <true|false>`
- `/authmepremium check <player>`
- `/authmepremium clear [player]`
- `/authmepremium setpremiumuuid <player> <true|false>`
- `/authmepremium setuuidmode <player> <default|cracked|premium|auto>`
- `/authmepremium migrateuuid <source> <target>`
- `/authmepremium reload`

Self-service: `/premium` (`/prem`), `/cracked` (`/crack`), `/premiumuuid` (`/uuid`), and `/migrate request|confirm|cancel`.

Bukkit trust: `/authmepremium pendingproxies`, `/authmepremium approveproxy <uuid>`, `/authmepremium rejectproxy <uuid>`.

## Permissions

- `authmepremium.admin`, default `op` in the Bukkit descriptor.
- `authmepremium.usage` for the proxy admin root.
- `authmepremium.premium`, `.cracked`, `.premiumuuid`, and `.migrate` for self-service commands.
- Self-service checks run only when `self-service-commands.require-permission: true`. The default is `false`.

## Troubleshooting

- `Backend auto-login blocked: proxy UUID is not approved.` Approve the UUID on that backend.
- Token mismatch, including after `Learned bridge token from proxy`: set one explicit token and restart.
- Premium action received without an AuthMe login: check ordering, log families, and mode matching.
- Auto-login retries exceeded: inspect the `auto-login.*` limits and the AuthMe flow.
- Folia `UnsupportedOperationException`: confirm you run the current universal JAR and see `FoliaAPI initialized`.
- Empty MySQL data: check the provider key shape and `authme_premium_profiles`. YAML and MEMORY are not shared stores.
- Never open backend firewall ports to fix trust.


## Related

- [AuthMe Premium product page](/plugins/authme-premium/)
- [Proxy/backend topology guide](/guides/authme-premium-topologies/)
- [Securing a proxy/backend link](/guides/secure-proxy-backend/)
- [Folia compatibility notes](/guides/folia-compatibility/)
- [Plugin troubleshooting workflow](/guides/plugin-troubleshooting-workflow/)

BlockLimiter caps block counts per chunk. Dense player-built structures cannot dominate load and persistence cost once a limit is set.

# ChatSentinel chat filtering and SocialSpy

URL: https://arkflame.com/docs/chatsentinel/
Updated: 2026-10-30

## What it does

ChatSentinel is a chat filter for Bukkit/Spigot, BungeeCord, and Velocity, built on one shared checking core. Bundled modules cover folder-based blacklists (`security`, `advertisement`, `offense`, `user`, `client`), capitalization, flood, similarity, cooldown, syntax, allowed characters, correction, server mute, and a join-location movement gate. SocialSpy covers private messages, signs, books, anvil renames, and commands. Alerts go to Discord webhooks and, optionally, Redis.

It does not punish anyone. Offense responses are a list of console commands under `punishments`. The config recommends LiteBans or AdvancedBans for mutes. Chat clear prints blank lines (`chat-snapshot.clear-lines: 128`). The repository states that message history is no longer stored.

## Requirements

- `plugin.yml` declares `api-version: "1.13"` and `folia-supported: true`. Soft dependencies: Essentials, EssentialsLite, ZelChat.
- A BungeeCord descriptor ships as `bungee.yml`. Velocity uses a `@Plugin` entrypoint compiled against Velocity API `3.4.0-SNAPSHOT`.
- Java 8 build target, compiled against Spigot API `1.19-R0.1-SNAPSHOT` and BungeeCord API `1.21-R0.4`.
- Redis is optional. Jedis is shaded and relocated. No database is used.
- Mute enforcement depends on an external punishment plugin.

## Install

Run the Maven build. The POM is a single `jar` module with the Bukkit, BungeeCord, and Velocity entrypoints. `plugin.yml` and `bungee.yml` sit in the same resources directory, so one jar holds all three entrypoints.

Put the jar in `plugins/` on the Bukkit server or proxy. On startup, missing `config.yml`, `messages.yml`, `blacklist.yml`, `whitelist.yml`, and nested filter files get created. `/chatsentinel reload` reloads config, messages, filters, and the online-player cache.

## Configure

Server mute defaults:

```yaml
server-mute:
  enabled: true
  muted: false
  bypass-permission: "chatsentinel.mute.bypass"
```

`blacklist.modules.<folder>.enabled` turns each folder-backed group on or off. `blacklist.warn.max: 3` sets warns before `punishments` run; `-1` disables that path. `blacklist.fake_message` is documented as ineffective on BungeeCord. `general.global-bypass-permission: "chatsentinel.bypass"` skips enforcement but not `correction` or `no-move-chat`, which are listed under `global-bypass-excluded-modules`. `no-move-chat` is backend-only because proxies cannot see movement.

For user regexes, `/chatsentinel regex add <moduleId> common|raw <text|regex>` appends to `blacklist/<moduleId>/custom.yml`. `common` builds an expression from plain text. `raw` validates a regex capped at 512 characters.

Velocity-specific:

```yaml
velocity:
  signed-chat-policy: "legacy-deny"
```

The bundled comment warns that `legacy-deny` may kick 1.19.1+ signed-chat clients. `warn-only` never changes the chat event.

## Commands

- `/chatsentinel help`, `status`, `selftest`, `reload`, `clear [reason]`, `notify`, `spy`
- `/chatsentinel module list|enable|disable|toggle <moduleId>`
- `/chatsentinel regex add <moduleId> common|raw <text|regex>`
- `/chatsentinel mutechat [on|off|toggle] [reason]`
- `/servermute [on|off|toggle] [reason]` with aliases `/muteall` and `/muteserver`
- `/autocorrect [on|off|toggle]` (player only)
- `/socialspy [module|status]`; `/socialspy menu` opens the Bukkit GUI

Aliases for `/chatsentinel` in `plugin.yml` include `autocorrect`, `correction`, `servermute`, `muteall`, `muteserver`, `socialspy`, and `sspy`. `status` requires `chatsentinel.help`; `selftest` requires `chatsentinel.admin`.

## Permissions

`chatsentinel.admin` grants the declared staff children: `help`, `reload`, `clear`, `notify`, `spy`, `module`, `regex.add`, `mute`, and the SocialSpy submodules. Also declared: `chatsentinel.mute.bypass`, `chatsentinel.bypass`, `chatsentinel.bypass.capitalization`, `chatsentinel.bypass.correction`, `chatsentinel.clear.bypass`, `chatsentinel.notify`, `chatsentinel.spy`, `chatsentinel.socialspy`, `chatsentinel.socialspy.messages`, `.signs`, `.books`, `.anvils`, and `.commands`.

`chatsentinel.mute` is used by the command service but is not declared as a standalone top-level permission in `plugin.yml`. It appears only as an admin child. `/autocorrect` does no permission check in the shared command service, so any player can toggle personal correction.

## Troubleshooting

- Kicks on Velocity after enabling `legacy-deny`: switch `signed-chat-policy` to `warn-only`. Detection still notifies.
- Punishments never run: `punishments` is empty, no mute plugin is installed, or `warn.max` has not been reached.
- Chat is still filtered for an operator: `chatsentinel.bypass` is the global gate, but correction and no-move-chat ignore it by design.
- `fake_message: true` on BungeeCord: the config comment says it does not work there.
- Filter changes ignored: user regexes go to `blacklist/user/custom.yml`. Check the startup compile report controlled by `filter-compile.notify-admins`.


## Related

- [ChatSentinel product page](/plugins/chatsentinel/)
- [Securing a proxy/backend link](/guides/secure-proxy-backend/)
- [FlameCord quick start](/docs/flamecord/)
- [VeloFlame quick start](/docs/veloflame/)
- [Plugin troubleshooting workflow](/guides/plugin-troubleshooting-workflow/)

# ExploitFixer quick start

URL: https://arkflame.com/docs/exploitfixer/
Updated: 2026-10-30

ExploitFixer inspects serverbound packets before they reach normal plugin handling. It ships 14 module files covering packet size limits, per-packet processing time, command blocking, book limits, and related crash vectors. HamsterAPI is the packet engine. PacketEvents and ProtocolLib are optional decoded-packet adapters.

## Requirements

- A Spigot, Paper, or Folia server. `plugin.yml` sets `api-version: "1.13"` and `folia-supported: true`. `config.yml` names all three as targets.
- **HamsterAPI installed and enabled.** `plugin.yml` lists it under `softdepend`, but startup returns early without it. Treat it as a hard dependency.
- HamsterAPI 0.3.5 or newer. Below that version the plugin logs a severe message but keeps starting.
- Optional decoded-packet adapters, built against PacketEvents 2.13.0 and ProtocolLib 5.3.0. Neither library is bundled or required.
- Java 8 build target.

## Install

1. Put the ExploitFixer jar in the server's `plugins/` directory.
2. Put HamsterAPI in the same directory and confirm it is enabled.
3. Deploy both on every Spigot/Paper/Folia server. The config banner reads `INSTALL THE PLUGIN ON ALL SPIGOT/PAPER/FOLIA SERVERS!`
4. Start the server and check the console for the missing-HamsterAPI message below.

## Configure

`config.yml` ships with these defaults:

```yaml
PacketHooks:
  packet-events: true
  protocol-lib: true
Settings:
  locale: "en"
  web: "discord.gg/gF36AT3"
discord-webhook:
  enabled: false
  url: "https://discord.com/api/webhooks/<redacted>"
Violations:
  cancel: 25
  reduce: 20
```

Per-module settings live in `plugins/ExploitFixer/modules/`. Real defaults include `max_size: 50kb` and `tab_complete_limit: 256` in `packet-limiter.yml`, plus `limit-per-chunk: 32` in `book-limit.yml`. PacketWatchdog's `cancel-packets` defaults to `false`. The shipped comment explains that cancelling movement packets can look to the player like an immediate disconnect. Punitive watchdog commands enforce a hard minimum of 100 VLS. `notify` works at any threshold.

`command-blocker.yml` exposes a `bypass-permission` string. Its default is `exploitfixer.commandblocker.bypass`.

## Commands

Root is `/exploitfixer`, alias `/ef`.

| Command | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `/ef` or `/ef help` | Command list |
| `/ef stats` | Player statistics |
| `/ef notifications` | Player-only toggle |
| `/ef reload` | Reload configuration |
| `/ef config` | Edits `user-config.yml` overrides with confirmation |
| `/ef logs [recent\|most] [page]` | Detection registry |
| `/ef checks` | Lists modules |
| `/ef checks <enable\|disable\|toggle> <module>` | Toggles one module |


## Permissions

| Node | Default | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `exploitfixer.bypass.packetwatcher` | `false` | Declared in `plugin.yml` |
| `exploitfixer.admin` | — | Checked in code; grant it explicitly |
| `exploitfixer.notifications` | — | Checked in code; grant it explicitly |
| `exploitfixer.commandblocker.bypass` | — | Module config default, not a manifest node |

Do not describe `exploitfixer.admin` as an op-granted manifest permission. It has no default.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause and diagnostic |
| --- | --- |
| Startup aborts | Console says `HamsterAPI is missing or disabled. ExploitFixer cannot start.` Install and enable HamsterAPI. |
| Severe version message | `HamsterAPI 0.3.5 or newer is required.` Startup still continues. |
| Players disconnect when packets are cancelled | PacketWatchdog's `cancel-packets` was enabled. The default `false` avoids dropping movement packets from the pipeline. |
| Adapter appears inactive | `PacketHooks.packet-events` or `protocol-lib` is `false`, or the library is not installed. |


## Related

- [ExploitFixer product page](/plugins/exploitfixer/)
- [Packet abuse guide](/guides/exploitfixer-packet-abuse/)
- [Diagnose lag before adding limiters](/guides/diagnose-lag-before-limiters/)
- [Plugin troubleshooting workflow](/guides/plugin-troubleshooting-workflow/)

# FairPlay quick start

URL: https://arkflame.com/docs/fairplay/
Updated: 2026-10-30

FairPlay is a combat-focused anticheat built around compensation, not punishment alone. Detection feeds mitigation, such as synthetic hit opportunities for a clean player against a flagged target. It also ships conventional check modules for aimbot, autoclicker, autototem, fastbreak, hitbox, killaura, scaffold, and timer.

## Requirements

- A Bukkit, Spigot, or Paper server. `plugin.yml` resolves `api-version` to `1.13` and `folia-supported` to `true`.
- **PacketEvents installed.** `plugin.yml` declares `depend: [packetevents]`. Startup will not proceed without it.
- Optional integrations declared as soft dependencies: LuckPerms, Geyser-Spigot, floodgate, GrimAC, Vulcan, NoCheatPlus, PolarLoader, Intave, Matrix, Spartan. It loads without GrimAC or Vulcan. Missing hooks are expected.
- Minecraft 1.8–1.21, with a Java 8 build target.
- Java 8 is the compiler source and target. The repo documents no runtime Java requirement beyond that.

## Install

No numbered install guide ships in the repo. What the source documents:

1. Build the reactor from the parent POM. Modules are `models`, `fairplay-api`, and `fairplay`.
2. Run `./build.sh`. It refuses to build without the real bundled model files. A failure reads `ERROR: Missing/empty bundled FairPlay model: <path>`. Recover them with `FAIRPLAY_MODELS_SOURCE_JAR=/path/to/FairPlay.jar ./build.sh` or `FAIRPLAY_MODELS_SOURCE_DIR=/path/to/plugins/FairPlay/models ./build.sh`.
3. Install only the FairPlay plugin jar in `plugins/`. Do not install the API jar as a plugin or shade its classes.
4. The first start writes `config.yml` into the plugin data folder. Training window output goes to `plugins/FairPlay/windows/global/<player>/<UTC-date-and-session>.json`.

## Configure

No YAML is bundled. The config is generated from annotated Java classes, and defaults come from field initializers. A missing path logs `[FairPlay] Missing config value for path '…'`.

```yaml
bedrock-check: true
show-cancel-messages: false
auto-update-models: true
player-logs-enabled: true
cancel-message-cooldown-ms: 60000
```

`machine-learning-training` only affects training error costs, not runtime detection. The deprecated `confirmation` and `client-tick-sync` blocks remain for compatibility with older configs.

## Commands

Root is `/fairplay`, aliases `/fp` and `/anticheat`.

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `/fp checks <enable\|disable\|toggle> <check\|category>` | Toggle checks |
| `/fp alerts <enable\|disable\|toggle\|inspect\|clear> [player]` | Alert subscriptions |
| `/fp punishments <list\|add\|remove\|clear> [value]` | Punishment rules |
| `/fp toggle <check\|category>` | Toggle a check or category |
| `/fp kick <enable\|disable\|toggle>` | Kick behavior |
| `/fp damagecancel <enable\|disable\|toggle>` | Damage cancellation |
| `/fp blockcancel <enable\|disable\|toggle>` | Block cancellation |
| `/fp ml <aim\|click>` | ML inspection |
| `/fp latency <player> <seconds 1..120>` | Latency handling |
| `/fp banwave run` | Run a ban wave |
| `/fp ml aim window record GLOBAL` | Start global AIM window recording |
| `/fp ml aim window stop` / `status` | Stop recording / inspect completion |

The global window commands require `fairplay.command.ml.global`, default operator.

## Permissions

Every node is declared with default `op`, except the exemptions: `fairplay.admin`, `fairplay.train`, `fairplay.check`, `fairplay.notify`, `fairplay.command.ml`, `fairplay.command.ml.global`, `fairplay.command.damagecancel`, `fairplay.command.blockcancel`, `fairplay.command.latency`, `fairplay.command.rotations`, and `fairplay.command.banwave`. The exemptions are `fairplay.exempt`, `fairplay.nosetback`, and `fairplay.nomodifypacket`, all default `false`.

`fairplay.command` appears in the README and as a child of several nodes. It has no standalone declaration or default in `plugin.yml`. Grant it explicitly if needed.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause and diagnostic |
| --- | --- |
| No GrimAC or Vulcan detection | Expected when neither plugin is installed. FairPlay still loads. |
| Missing config warning | `[FairPlay] Missing config value for path '…'`. The generated config lacks that key. |
| Build stops on models | `Missing/empty bundled FairPlay model`. Restore the trained `.nn` assets. Do not substitute blank artifacts. |
| Reach diagnostics look ambiguous | `reach-increase applied`, `range`, `aim`, `visibility_*`, and `candidate` do not prove a hit. Only `reach-increase damage-applied` confirms a `MONITOR`-confirmed applied hit. |


## Related

- [FairPlay product page](/plugins/fairplay/)
- [FairPlay false positives](/guides/fairplay-false-positives/)
- [ExploitFixer quick start](/docs/exploitfixer/)
- [SMP punishments](/docs/smp-punishments/)
- [Plugin troubleshooting workflow](/guides/plugin-troubleshooting-workflow/)

# FlameCord quick start

URL: https://arkflame.com/docs/flamecord/
Updated: 2026-10-30

FlameCord is a BungeeCord/Waterfall fork that replaces the proxy jar. It adds antibot checks, packet limits, and a firewall module on top of the upstream proxy, and tracks Waterfall changes as needed.

## Requirements

- A Linux host if the firewall module stays enabled. `antibot.firewall.ipset` defaults to `true`. Startup runs `apt install iptables -y`, `apt install ipset -y`, `ipset create flamecord hash:ip timeout <time>`, and an `iptables -t raw -I PREROUTING` drop rule for the `flamecord` set. This needs root.
- No plugin dependencies. FlameCord is a standalone proxy replacement, not a plugin.
- Java 17 is the proxy module's Maven compiler release and Java 11 the bootstrap's. These are compile targets. The README states no runtime Java version.

The proxy's protocol table lists `1.8.x` through `1.21.x` plus `26.x`, ending at `MINECRAFT_26_3`. The project version is `26.1-R0.1-SNAPSHOT`.

## Install

1. Build or obtain `FlameCord.jar`. The bootstrap module sets `finalName` to `FlameCord` and main class `net.md_5.bungee.Bootstrap`.
2. Place the jar in the proxy directory and run it. The README says to drag and drop it into the server folder.
3. Keep `iptables` and `ipset` installed, and run as root, if you leave `antibot.firewall.ipset: true`.
4. The first start generates `flamecord.yml` and `modules.yml`. Missing keys are appended on later loads with `setIfUnexistant`.

No FlameCord component goes on backends.

## Configure

Real defaults from `flamecord.yml`:

```yaml
antibot:
  accounts:
    enabled: true
    limit: 3
  latency:
    limit: 900
  country:
    blacklist: ["CN", "HK", "RU", "IN", "TH", "ID", "DZ", "VN", "IR", "PK"]
  firewall:
    enabled: true
    ipset: true
    time: 60
  ratelimit:
    connections-per-second: 3
  packets:
    vls-to-kick: 100.0
    vls-to-cancel: 25.0
balancer:
  enabled: false
```

The firewall thread also destroys and recreates the `flamecord` ipset at startup, and removes the iptables rule at shutdown. The repository does not state what happens when `apt`, `ipset`, or `iptables` fail. Verify the rule exists rather than assuming the module is active.

`modules.yml` toggles upstream Bungee modules: `alert`, `find`, `ip`, `list`, `perms`, `reload`, `send`, `server`, and `reconnect`. All default to `true` except `reconnect`.

## Commands and permissions

FlameCord uses the upstream Bungee command set. The `modules.yml` flags enable `alert`, `find`, `ip`, `list`, `perms`, `reload`, `send`, `server`, and `reconnect`.

FlameCord declares **no permission nodes**. The module ships no `plugin.yml` or equivalent descriptor. Do not copy upstream Bungee permission nodes into a FlameCord setup and expect them to be verified here.

## Troubleshooting

The repository has **no troubleshooting document or section**. The only operational failure path visible in source is the firewall startup sequence. The `apt`, `ipset`, and `iptables` commands run on a background thread, gated by `antibot.firewall.ipset`. Failure handling is not defined in the repo. Source shows the exact commands it attempts. Verify on the host that they took effect.


## Related

- [FlameCord product page](/plugins/flamecord/)
- [VeloFlame quick start](/docs/veloflame/)
- [FlameCord vs VeloFlame](/guides/flamecord-vs-veloflame/)
- [Secure proxy and backend setup](/guides/secure-proxy-backend/)
- [Diagnose lag before adding limiters](/guides/diagnose-lag-before-limiters/)

# FlameStack dropped-item stacking

URL: https://arkflame.com/docs/flamestack/
Updated: 2026-10-30

## What it does

FlameStack merges dropped items without sweeping worlds or entities. Lifecycle events fill a concurrent world/chunk/16-block-section index. One global bounded async coordinator consumes a server-wide raw ticket budget per run. Merge reservations carry a TTL. Committed transactions are compensated, not discarded. Bukkit entity reads and writes run on the item's entity scheduler, or on the Bukkit main scheduler outside Folia.

The aggregate amount is virtual. The physical dropped stack stays at a vanilla-safe projection. When a player or hopper picks it up, the logical amount moves through managed inventory paths, and the vanilla pickup event is cancelled. Non-virtual items keep vanilla pickup behavior. FlameStack is not a clear-lag tool, an entity limiter, or a chunk optimizer.

## Requirements

- Java 8 bytecode. `pom.xml` sets `maven.compiler.release` to 8.
- `plugin.yml` declares `api-version: 1.13` and `folia-supported: true`. The README states Bukkit/Spigot/Paper API 1.13+.
- Adventure and MiniMessage are shaded and relocated. The plugin declares no external plugin dependency.
- Java 8 runtime.

## Install

The README documents:

```bash
mvn clean test package
```

The README names the output `target/FlameStack-0.0.3.jar`, but `pom.xml` and `plugin.yml` both declare `1.0.1`. Confirm the artifact from the build output or jar manifest, not the README filename.

Place the jar in `plugins/` and start the server. No proxy component exists. The first start creates `config.yml`. `/flamestack reload` re-reads it.

## Configure

```yaml
stacking:
  max-stack-size: 2304
  merge-radius: 8.0
  scan-interval-ticks: 20
  scan-budget-per-run: 64
  max-active-merge-reservations: 64
  reservation-timeout-millis: 10000
```

`candidate-scan-limit-per-item` defaults to `256`, is clamped to `1..2048`, and must be at least `candidate-limit-per-item` (default `64`). The comments call `scan-budget-per-run` a server-wide raw ticket budget, not a per-shard cap. Stale or ineligible tickets are filtered before a merge decision.

`allow_list` defaults to `enabled: true`, `mode: blacklist`, with `BARRIER`. With `trigger.enabled: true` and `respect-vanilla-max-stack: true`, stone `32 + 32` stays untouched, and `32 + 33` can merge. Non-stackable items become eligible at `1 + 1`. `display.enabled: true` and `always-visible: true` show the floating amount, formatted with the MiniMessage `display.format`. Invalid material names are logged and ignored.

`debug: false` enables bounded diagnostics for registration, index lookup, reservations, and merge decisions. The config says to keep it off in normal operation.

## Commands

`/flamestack [help|reload|stats]`, with aliases `/fs` and `/fstack`.

`/flamestack stats` prints the platform, tracked items, indexed sections, and active merge reservations, using the labels under `messages.stats`.

## Permissions

- `flamestack.admin` (default `op`) grants `flamestack.reload` and `flamestack.stats`.
- `flamestack.reload` (default `op`) reloads configuration.
- `flamestack.stats` (default `op`) shows runtime statistics.

## Troubleshooting

- No merges: check `trigger.enabled`, `allow_list.mode`, `stacking.max-stack-size`, and whether the material is excluded.
- Items below the vanilla maximum do not merge: expected while `respect-vanilla-max-stack: true`.
- Merge bursts stall: `max-active-merge-reservations: 64` caps concurrent reservations. The coordinator filters raw tickets before deciding.
- Suspect a duplicate jar: the README and POM disagree on version. Confirm from the jar manifest or build output.
- Invalid material names disappear from `allow_list`: the README says they are logged and ignored. `MaterialUtil.get` falls back to `Material.AIR` rather than returning null.


## Related

- [FlameStack product page](/plugins/flamestack/)
- [Diagnose lag before adding limiters](/guides/diagnose-lag-before-limiters/)
- [Folia compatibility notes](/guides/folia-compatibility/)
- [RedstoneLimiter quick start](/docs/redstonelimiter/)
- [Plugin troubleshooting workflow](/guides/plugin-troubleshooting-workflow/)

# RedstoneLimiter configuration and monitor mode

URL: https://arkflame.com/docs/redstonelimiter/
Updated: 2026-10-30

## What it does

RedstoneLimiter counts observable redstone activity per spatial scope. It blocks activity when a scope exceeds its period maximum. It observes redstone transitions (`BlockRedstoneEvent`), observers (`BlockPhysicsEvent`), dispensers and droppers (`BlockDispenseEvent`), and pistons (extend and retract). Piston push length is checked separately with `max_piston_push`, default `12`.

Signals flow `Block -> Subchunk -> Chunk -> Region`. An activation is recorded at every scope it reaches. The first blocking scope returns. Material overrides exist at block scope, with `DEFAULT` as the only fallback. `GLOBAL` is legacy-only.

Quarantine is manual.

## Requirements

- A Bukkit/Spigot-family server. `plugin.yml` declares `api-version: 1.13` and `folia-supported: true`.
- No plugin dependencies. The file has no `depend` or `softdepend` entries.
- Redis only when `notifications.cross_server.enabled` is on. It ships `false`.
- The POM compiles Java 8 against `spigot-api 1.8.8`. Runtime code uses modern Chunk/Region APIs and shaded Adventure, so the compile target is not a server floor.


## Install

Install from the current [BuiltByBit release](https://builtbybit.com/resources/redstonelimiter-smart-redstone-limiter.23133/). Place the jar in your server's plugins directory and start the server. The listing handles distribution and updates.

## Configure

The configuration contract is version 7. Startup and reload migrate older files, then save.

- Block maxima are per material: `DEFAULT: 5`, `REDSTONE_WIRE: 12`. Subchunks `96`, chunks `1024`, regions `96`.
- Every scope has `period.duration-millis` `5000`, `period.sustain-millis` `2000`, and `period.sliding: true`.
- `enabled: false` records telemetry without blocking. `max-activations: 0` means unlimited.
- A region is a fixed 32x32-chunk area, not a Folia scheduler region.

```yaml
config-version: 7
monitor: false
anti-lag:
  preset: "STRICT"
  tps-scaling:
    enabled: true
blocks:
  max-activations:
    DEFAULT: 5
    REDSTONE_WIRE: 12
chunks:
  max-activations: 1024
max_piston_push: 12
```

Presets multiply max activations only: `STRICT` `1.0x`, `BALANCED` `1.5x`, `LENIENT` `2.0x`. Duration and sustain do not change. TPS scaling also multiplies the maxima: `1.0x` at or below `16.0` TPS, `2.0x` at or above `19.5`, linear in between.

Monitor mode (`monitor: true`) bypasses enforcement and its effects. It keeps detection, verdicts, throttled notifications and telemetry, and exemptions. Quarantine and max piston push become alerts. The comparator/trapdoor guard is bypassed. Notifications then mean "would block". `/rl reload` applies it.

## Commands

`/redstonelimiter` and `/rl` are equivalent.

| Command | Behavior | Permission |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/rl` | Aggregate statistics | `redstonelimiter.stats` |
| `/rl block` | Top block danger zones | `redstonelimiter.stats` |
| `/rl subchunk` | Top subchunk danger zones | `redstonelimiter.stats` |
| `/rl chunk` | Top chunk danger zones | `redstonelimiter.stats` |
| `/rl chunk <world> <chunk-x> <chunk-z>` | Opens the chunk's Blocks page; player only | `redstonelimiter.stats` |
| `/rl region` | Top region danger zones | `redstonelimiter.stats` |
| `/rl gui` | Control panel; `/rl menu` still works | `redstonelimiter.admin` |
| `/rl reload` | Reloads config after saved GUI changes | `redstonelimiter.reload` |
| `/rl tp <world> <x> <y> <z>` | Teleports to a notification target; player only | — |
| `/rl notifications` | Toggles personal notifications | notification permission |
| `/rl visit <server> <world> <x> <y> <z>` | Redis/proxy cross-server travel | notification permission |

## Permissions

All four descriptor nodes default to `op`:

- `redstonelimiter.admin` opens the control panel.
- `redstonelimiter.stats` reads statistics.
- `redstonelimiter.reload` reloads configuration.
- `redstonelimiter.notify` receives notifications. Configurable through `notifications.permission`.

## Troubleshooting

- **Legitimate circuits throttled.** Raise maxima, duration, or sustain. Or change the preset, or whitelist the chunk.
- **Observer activity not cancelled.** Observer physics is uncancellable telemetry.
- **Contraptions not analyzed.** Only piston push length is checked.
- **TPS reads unavailable.** A missing or invalid TPS falls back to the `1.0x` multiplier.
- **Old keys.** Version 7 migration maps `anti-lag.sliding-window.*` to per-scope periods and `blocks.threshold.*` to `max-activations.*`. Whitelist and quarantine lists survive.
- **Folia.** Player and entity work uses `runTaskForEntity`, region work uses `runTaskForRegion`, and global work uses the Folia scheduler when available.

# SMP Lifesteal commands and configuration

URL: https://arkflame.com/docs/smp-lifesteal/
Updated: 2026-10-30

## What it does

SMP Lifesteal is a lifesteal core built around lives, heart items, withdrawal, and rebirth. On player death, the attacker gains a life by default. If the attacker is already at maximum, the heart drops instead. Entity and natural deaths can also drop hearts. First-join protection defaults to `10m`.

The repository also ships compatibility grammar for ZelSteal and LifeStealZ command shapes, plus PlaceholderAPI expansions named `smplifesteal` and `zelsteal`. It is not a general economy or punishment suite.

## Requirements

- Bukkit/Spigot/Paper/Purpur/Folia. `plugin.yml` declares `folia-supported: true`.
- Minecraft `1.8.8` through `1.21.x`, as stated in `README.md`.
- Java 8 source/target in the POM. That is a build target, not a runtime guarantee.
- Optional soft dependencies: PlaceholderAPI, WorldGuard, Vault, AxAuctions.
- A storage backend: local YAML files, SQLite, or MySQL. MySQL can use local YAML as a shadow and fallback.

## Build and storage

`README.md` documents:

```bash
mvn test
mvn -DskipTests package
```

The output is `target/smplifesteal-1.1.5.jar`. The README calls SQLite the default at `plugins/SMPLifesteal/storage.db`, but the bundled `settings.yml` sets `database-type: yml`. The SQLite path applies only after you switch the type. `settings.yml` also sets `fallback.use-local-yml-when-sql-down: true`, while `allow-default-player-when-sql-down-and-no-local-file` stays `false`.

Storage values are `yml`, `sqlite`, and `mysql`. With `local-yml.shadow-sql-storage: true`, SQL-backed installs also write local YAML copies.

## Configure

A minimal excerpt of real keys:

```yaml
Database-Settings:
  database-type: sqlite
  sqlite:
    file: data/storage.db
Lives-Settings:
  default-lives: 10
  default-max-lives: 20
  withdraw:
    min-lives-after-withdraw: 1
    default-amount: 1
  rebirth:
    lives-to-reset-to: 10
```

Related defaults in the same file:

- `health-points-per-life: 2.0`, with `clamp-health-on-apply: true`.
- `ban-time: 1w`. Life bans are checked at pre-login by default.
- `withdraw.max-amount-per-command: 64`; `drop-if-inventory-full: false`.
- `rebirth.max-rebirths: 10` and `max-life-increase: 1`.
- Death rewards: `by-player.enabled: true`, `attacker-gains-life: true`, `drop-when-attacker-maxed: true`. Entity and natural drops are also enabled.
- Same-victim reward cooldowns default to `15m` for player, entity, and natural deaths.
- `Anti-Alt-Settings.enabled: true`. Replace the shipped `ip-hash-salt` placeholder with a unique random value before you enable detection in production.
- `Anti-Dupe-Settings.enabled: false`. Enabling it prevents heart reuse but disables heart stacking, per the file's own comment.

`Cross-Server.enabled` is `false`. Redis is needed only when cross-server sync is on.

## Commands

Root command `/lifesteal` has aliases `smplifesteal`, `lives`, and `live`:

- `/withdraw [amount]` converts lives into heart items.
- `/rebirth` resets lives and adds permanent maximum lives when eligible.
- `/lifesteal admin reload`
- `/lifesteal admin info [player]`
- `/lifesteal admin setlives|addlives|removelives <player> <amount>`
- `/lifesteal admin setmaxlives|addmaxlives|removemaxlives <player> <amount>`
- `/lifesteal admin setrebirths <player> <amount>`
- `/lifesteal admin ban <player> [duration]` and `unban <player>`
- `/lifesteal admin giveheart <player> [type]`
- `/lifesteal admin convert <source> [--dry-run|--apply]`

ZelSteal-shaped commands such as `/zelsteal lives` and `/zelsteal withdraw` map onto the same operations.

## Permissions

Player nodes default to `true`: `lifesteal.use`, `lifesteal.withdraw`, `lifesteal.rebirth`. `lifesteal.view.others` defaults to `op`.

Admin nodes default to `op`: `lifesteal.admin` plus `reload`, `setlives`, `addlives`, `removelives`, `setmaxlives`, `addmaxlives`, `setrebirths`, `ban`, `unban`, `giveheart`, `info`, and `convert`.

Notification nodes `lifesteal.antialt.notify` and `lifesteal.antidupe.notify` default to `op`. The descriptor also declares parallel `smplifesteal.*` and `zelsteal.*` nodes for compatibility. It also declares `lifesteal.bypass.firstjoin`, `antialt`, `antidupe`, and `life-ban` nodes, all defaulting to `op`.

## Troubleshooting

- **Placeholders render literally.** Restart after installing the expansion, confirm PlaceholderAPI is present, and run `/papi reload`.
- **WorldGuard hook missing.** Check startup for the hook line and load order. On Folia, confirm the scheduler bridge initialized.
- **SQL unavailable.** The plugin falls back to local YAML when `use-local-yml-when-sql-down` is true. Check credentials and connectivity rather than deleting data.
- **Duplicate heart message.** Expected while anti-dupe is enabled, because hearts are single-use records. It ships disabled, which also permits stacking.
- **Anti-alt misses accounts.** Change the salt from the placeholder and confirm players arrive with consistent IPs. VPNs can create false relations.
- **Folia scheduler warnings.** Update the plugin and review `Advanced-Settings.scheduler-pool-size`.

- [Plugin troubleshooting workflow](/guides/plugin-troubleshooting-workflow/)

# SMP Punishments operations and configuration

URL: https://arkflame.com/docs/smp-punishments/
Updated: 2026-10-30

## What it does

SMP Punishments covers bans, IP bans, mutes, kicks, freezes, screenshares, totem checks, warnings, reports, and staff lookup tools. It ships SQLite and MySQL storage with HikariCP. Join-ban checks run async through `AsyncPlayerPreLoginEvent`. Optional MySQL `sync_events` propagate changes across servers. It also has PlaceholderAPI and Simple Voice Chat hooks, Discord webhook notifications, and player and reason selector GUIs.

The repository uses conservative Bukkit API calls. It uses reflection for Folia scheduling and modern player-head ownership. It is a moderation suite, not a proxy or authentication plugin.

## Requirements

- A Bukkit/Spigot-family server. `plugin.yml` declares `api-version: 1.13` and `folia-supported: true`.
- Optional soft dependencies: PlaceholderAPI and `voicechat`. The voice hook loads only when Simple Voice Chat is present.
- SQLite for single-server installs, or MySQL when multi-server propagation is needed. The README states that SQLite stays local-only.

## Build and storage

Build with `mvn -DskipTests package`. Place the jar in your server's plugins directory and start the server. The first run generates `config.yml`.

Defaults in `config.yml`:

- `storage.type: SQLITE` with `sqlite-file: data.db`.
- `storage.write-queue.flush-on-submit: true` and `max-writes-per-flush: 256`.
- `network.enabled: false`. Multi-server sync targets MySQL.
- Existing tables upgrade on startup by detecting missing tables, columns, and indexes. The README calls the migration idempotent and says rows are preserved.

## Configure

A minimal excerpt of real keys:

```yaml
storage:
  type: SQLITE
  sqlite-file: data.db
network:
  enabled: false
  server-id: ""
warnings:
  strike-period: "24h"
  max-strikes: 3
  same-target-cooldown: "1m"
  punishment:
    enabled: true
    type: BAN
    duration: "1d"
check-join-ban-on-prelogin: true
```

Other defaults worth knowing:

- `freeze-block-movement: true`.
- `mute.mode: CANCEL`. The command filter is a `BLACKLIST` containing `/msg`, `/tell`, `/w`, `/r`, `/reply`, and `/mail send`.
- `limits.default-max-duration: "1y"`, with per-permission caps of `30d`, `90d`, `180d`, and `365d`.
- `security.dupeip.hide-ips: true`, `max-accounts: 50`, `max-ips: 50`.
- Discord webhook defaults: `enabled: false`, an empty `url`, and event toggles for bans, kicks, and warns. The URL is a secret. Keep it out of commits and tickets. Silent punishments still reach the webhook. The old `hooks.warning-webhook` block remains a runtime fallback.

Warnings use a target-wide rolling window. Strikes are computed, not entered by hand. Crossing `max-strikes` applies the configured punishment. Staff with `smppunishments.bypass.warncooldown` skip the same-target cooldown.

## Commands

Declared roots and subcommands:

- `/ban`, `/tempban`, `/banip` (aliases `/ban-ip`, `/ipban`), `/unban` (`/pardon`), `/unbanip`
- `/mute`, `/tempmute`, `/unmute`, `/kick`, `/freeze` (`/stopchat`)
- `/screenshare` (`/ss`), `/totemcheck` (`/totemtest`, `/autototemcheck`)
- `/warn <player> [reason...]`, `/reports`
- `/history` (`/punhistory`), `/banhistory`, `/mutehistory`
- `/banlist` (`/listbans`), `/mutelist` (`/listmutes`), `/clearbans`, `/clearmutes`
- `/searchid` (`/puninfo`, `/baninfo`, `/muteinfo`)
- `/dupeip` (`/alts`) for shared-IP lookup
- `/smppunishments` (`/punishments`, `/sp`, `/smpp`) with `reload`
- `/notify` (permission `smppunishments.notify`)

The README omits `tempban`, `tempmute`, `screenshare`, `totemcheck`, and `notify`, but `plugin.yml` declares them.

## Permissions

Core: `smppunishments.*`. `smppunishments.admin` covers the main command and reload. `smppunishments.notify` covers broadcasts.

Punishments: `smppunishments.ban`, `tempban`, `banip`, `unban`, `unbanip`, `mute`, `tempmute`, `unmute`, `kick`, `freeze`, `warn`, `reports`, `screenshare`, `totemcheck`.

History and lookup: `history`, `history.ban`, `history.mute`, `searchid`, `list.bans`, `list.mutes`, `clear.bans`, `clear.mutes`, `dupeip`, and `dupeip.viewip`.

Bypass: `bypass.mute`, `bypass.freeze`, `bypass.warncooldown`, plus `bypass.illegalitems` and the `silent` / `notify.silent` nodes. Duration and limits: `duration.permanent`, `unlimited.ban`, `unlimited.mute`, `group.unlimited`. GUI: `smppunishments.gui`, `stats`.

Except for `smppunishments.*`, descriptor nodes default to `op`.

## Troubleshooting

- **Webhook silent.** Only bans, kicks, and warns are delivered. Check `hooks.discord-webhook.enabled` and the per-event toggles. Run `/smppunishments reload` after edits.
- **Webhook URL leaked.** Rotate it in Discord and replace the config value. Do not paste it into reports.
- **Sync not working.** Multi-server sync expects MySQL. Check `network.enabled`, `server-id`, and the shared database. SQLite stays local.
- **Pool timeouts.** Diagnostics include active, idle, total, and waiting connection counts when Hikari metrics are available.
- **Voice mute missing.** The hook loads only when the `voicechat` plugin is present.
