# SMP Regions resets, flags and commands

URL: https://arkflame.com/docs/smp-regions/
Updated: 2026-10-30

## What it does

SMP Regions manages cuboid regions whose player-made changes reset on a timer. It protects original map blocks, tracks temporary placements and breaks, persists the temporal cache, and skips resets when nothing changed. Regions resolve per world. When several match, the higher `priority` wins per flag. `__global__` provides a per-world fallback. The same region name may exist in different worlds.

Region files live under `plugins/SMPRegions/regions/<world>/<region>.yml`. Tracked blocks live under `cache/temporal_blocks/<world>/<x_y_z>.yml`. The plugin keeps its own region index and reset model and does not require WorldGuard. `/rg` is registered only when WorldGuard is absent.

## Requirements

- Bukkit/Spigot/Paper/Folia. `plugin.yml` declares `api-version: 1.13` and `folia-supported: true`.
- The README states a `1.8 -> 1.21.11` target and a Java 8 source target. That is a compatibility target, not a tested matrix.
- Optional soft dependencies: DecentHolograms, FancyHolograms, and `packetevents`.
- PacketEvents `2.13.0` is required only for local `time-lock` client-time simulation. It is not bundled.
- WorldGuard is not required for protection checks.

## Install

The README documents `mvn clean install`, which publishes the artifact to the local Maven repository. It names `target/SMPRegions-1.2.1.jar`. `pom.xml` declares `1.2.3`, and `CHANGELOG.md` stops at `1.2.0`. Confirm the built jar name from the build output.

Drop the jar in `plugins/` and start the server. The jar ships `config.yml`, `lang/`, and a disabled `regions/world/example-region.yml`. Resets, saves, and reloads operate on files under the data folder.

## Configure

A real region file:

```yaml
name: example-region
enabled: false
priority: 0
reset-every: 5
world: world
flags:
  pvp: deny
  use-elytra: deny
  block-break: deny
  temporal-block-place: allow
  temporal-block-break: allow
```

`reset-every` is in minutes. `0` disables automatic resets for that region. Manual `/smprg reset` and individual temporal timers still work. Temporal flags are evaluated first and are actor-independent. Owners, members, operators, and `smpregions.bypass` do not bypass an allowed temporal route. A denied or unset temporal flag falls through to permanent `block-place` or `block-break`. `entity_place` is independent and has no temporal mode.

Global defaults include `general.max-reset-blocks-per-tick: 20`, `reset-check-interval-seconds: 60`, `build-denied-adventure-mode: true`, and `temporal-block.restore-block-physics: false`. `chunk-unload: deny` keeps whole intersected chunks loaded via native tickets where the runtime supports them. Legacy runtimes log one warning and leave retention inactive. `__global__` rejects a non-unset `chunk-unload`.

## Commands

Base command `/smprg`, aliases `/smpregions` and `/smpr`.

- `/smprg wand`, `create`, `redefine` (`update`, `move`), `delete` (`remove`), `info`, `priority`
- `/smprg reset`, `list`, `flags`, `flag <region> <flag> <value|unset>`
- `/smprg load`, `save`, `reload`

Most accept `[-w <world>]`. `save` forces an immediate write.

## Permissions

`smpregions.admin` grants every node. Command nodes include `smpregions.command.use`, `.reload`, `.flag`, `.flags`, `.info`, `.list`, `.create`, `.delete`, `.redefine`, `.priority`, `.reset`, `.wand`, `.save`, and `.load`. `smpregions.bypass` bypasses gameplay restrictions after temporal evaluation.

Region-scoped nodes such as `smpregions.region.info.owner`, `smpregions.region.flag.member`, `smpregions.region.addmember.member`, `smpregions.region.delete.owner`, and `smpregions.region.redefine.owner` default to `false`. `smpregions.command.owner` and `smpregions.command.member` default to `true`.

## Troubleshooting

- An owner or op can still place tracked blocks: the temporal route is intentionally actor-independent.
- Local `time-lock` does nothing: PacketEvents is absent, or the lock is global. Local mode never changes world time.
- Chunk retention is inactive: the runtime lacks native chunk tickets, so the plugin logs one warning.
- A reset misses complex block data: v1 preserves inventories and front sign lines, not all block-entity metadata.
- Physics or liquid flags seem reserved but do nothing: the README calls them inactive in v1, and `use-physics-event` defaults to `false`.
- A region never resets automatically: `reset-every: 0` disables the timer.

# StaffModeX staff mode, vanish and reports

URL: https://arkflame.com/docs/staffmodex/
Updated: 2026-10-30

## What it does

StaffModeX is a Bukkit staff-management plugin. It covers staff mode with inventory and location restoration, vanish, local or networked staff chat, HelpOp, freeze, player examination, reports, warnings, moderation action menus, identity lookups, notes, audit logs, inventory backups, item scans, staff statistics, chat moderation, and diagnostics. It also ships BungeeCord and Velocity bridge modules.

It does not implement kick, ban, mute, or WorldEdit commands. `/moderate` and configured action menus dispatch administrator-supplied console commands. The plugin does not provide those punishments itself.

Network mode is `AUTO`, `PROXY`, `REDIS`, or `LOCAL`. Proxy transport uses `staffmodex:network`. Redis is optional. Reports and warnings use local YAML by default and MySQL when enabled.

## Requirements

- Bukkit-side `plugin.yml` declares `api-version: '1.13'` and `folia-supported: true`. Source and target are Java 8.
- Soft dependencies: PlaceholderAPI and PremiumVanish.
- Optional MySQL and Redis. Proxy modules compile against BungeeCord API `1.21-R0.4` and Velocity API `3.4.0`.
- Maven modules: `common`, `bukkit`, `bungee`, `velocity`, `universal`.
- Bukkit API 1.13.

## Install

Build with Maven. Module `finalName`s produce `StaffModeX.jar` for Bukkit and the universal module, `StaffModeX-Bungee.jar`, and `StaffModeX-Velocity.jar`. The universal build copies its jar to the root `target/StaffModeX.jar`.

Place the Bukkit jar in `plugins/`. If you use proxy features, place the matching proxy jar in the proxy's plugin directory. Bukkit uses these files under `plugins/StaffModeX/`: `config.yml`, `commands.yml`, `messages.yml`, `webhooks.yml`, `inventories.yml`, `infractions/`, and `ips/`. Proxy modules use `proxy-config.yml`, `proxy-messages.yml`, and `proxy-webhooks.yml`.

## Configure

```yaml
network:
  mode: AUTO
  proxy-channel: "staffmodex:network"
  dedupe-cache-size: 2048
  dedupe-ttl-seconds: 30
mysql:
  enabled: false
```

`staff-command-opens-staffmode: true` makes bare `/staff` toggle staff mode. `/staff list` still opens the list. Command topology is startup-owned. `commands.yml` controls `enabled`, aliases, permission, usage, and conflict policy. Changes need a full restart. `commands.skip-if-conflict: true` keeps foreign commands. `mysql` and `redis` both default to `false`. With MySQL off, local YAML stores reports, warnings, and IPs.

`messages.yml` selects `format: minimessage` or `legacy`. A missing or blank `format` falls back to `text-format`. An invalid value logs one warning and uses legacy. Existing runtime files are not migrated automatically. In MiniMessage, literal `<player>`-style text must be escaped.

## Commands

Core commands: `/staffmode` (`/mod`), `/vanish` (`/v`), `/staffchat` (`/sc`), `/helpop`, `/freeze`, `/examine` (`/invsee`), `/report`, `/warn`, `/reports`, `/warnings`, `/infractions`, `/ip` (`/iplog`), `/staff`, and `/staffmodex reload`.

Feature and command gates apply. `/freeze` needs `freeze.enabled`. `/helpop` needs both `helpop.enabled` and `commands.helpop.enabled`. `/vanish` needs `commands.vanish.enabled`. Other commands, such as `/moderate`, `/alts`, `/notes`, `/activity`, `/invbackups`, `/chatcontrol`, and `/serverinfo`, are enabled by default and documented in `commands.yml`.

## Permissions

Exact nodes include `staffmodex.admin`, `staffmodex.staffmode`, `staffmodex.staffchat`, `staffmodex.vanish`, `staffmodex.vanish.see`, `staffmodex.freeze`, `staffmodex.ip`, `staffmodex.warning`, `staffmodex.report`, `staffmodex.helpop`, `staffmodex.examine`, `staffmodex.infractions`, `staffmodex.moderation`, `staffmodex.manage`, `staffmodex.teleport`, `staffmodex.heal`, `staffmodex.chat.manage`, and `staffmodex.socialspy`.

Bypass nodes include `staffmodex.freeze.bypass`, `staffmodex.vanish.pvp`, `staffmodex.inventory.bypass`, and `staffmodex.bypass.cooldown`. The full command-to-node mapping is in `docs/commands-and-permissions.md`. Action-specific nodes extend `staffmodex.moderation` with `.warning`, `.kick`, `.mute`, `.tempban`, and `.ban`.

## Troubleshooting

- A new command or alias does not appear: command topology is startup-owned. Restart instead of running `/staffmodex reload`.
- Reload does not update proxy files, MySQL, or Redis connections: reload covers Bukkit YAML, messages, and webhooks only.
- Messages show raw tags: the file's `format` may still be `legacy`, or MiniMessage literal placeholders are unescaped.
- Reports or warnings vanish after switching storage: MySQL is disabled or not initialized. Local files live under `infractions/`.
- `/staff` opens the list instead of toggling: `staff-command-opens-staffmode` is false.
- Expecting `/ban` or `/mute`: not implemented. Only configured moderation actions dispatch console commands.

- [Securing a proxy/backend link](/guides/secure-proxy-backend/)
- [Plugin troubleshooting workflow](/guides/plugin-troubleshooting-workflow/)

# VeloFlame quick start

URL: https://arkflame.com/docs/veloflame/
Updated: 2026-10-30

VeloFlame is a Velocity proxy fork. It adds antibot checks, connection rate limits, a firewall module, and whitelist and maintenance commands for admins. Internally the project is `velocity-ctd`. Its README is upstream Velocity-CTD text, not VeloFlame documentation.

## Requirements

- Root or `CAP_NET_ADMIN` on Linux when `firewall.ipset` stays `true`, the default. The config notes that `ipset` and `iptables` are required. If setup fails, the Java-side cache still works.
- No plugin dependency descriptor. VeloFlame replaces the proxy.
- Java 25 build toolchain.

The protocol API declares `MINIMUM_VERSION = MINECRAFT_1_7_2` and a maximum at `MINECRAFT_26_3`. The declared range is 1.7.2 through 26.3.

Two version strings disagree. Gradle reports `4.2.1-SNAPSHOT`, while `VeloFlame.java` reports internal version `1.4.9`.

## Install

1. Build with the Gradle wrapper: `./gradlew build`.
2. Take the shaded proxy jar from `proxy/build/libs`. The produced file is **`VeloFlame-Lite.jar`**, hard-coded in `proxy/build.gradle.kts`.
3. Run it. A default `veloflame.toml` is generated alongside the core `velocity.toml`.
4. If `firewall.ipset` remains `true`, install `ipset` and `iptables` and run with root or `CAP_NET_ADMIN`.

**Artifact-name drift:** the README says `-all`. This build emits `VeloFlame-Lite.jar`.

## Configure

Real defaults from `default-veloflame.toml`:

```toml
config-version = "0.0.8"

[firewall]
enabled = true
duration = 60
ipset = true

[ratelimit]
connections = 3
connections-period = 5

[packet-guard]
serverbound-unknown-play-max-packet-size = 204800
```

Core proxy settings such as bind address, servers, and forwarding stay in `velocity.toml`. The `[limbo]` section is marked VeloFlame PRO only and defaults to `enabled = true`. Its default global whitelist includes localhost and private addresses. Remove those entries on a test instance, or the limbo check never sees your connection. `[advanced] seamless-server-switching` defaults to `false`. The config warns to enable it only when backends use compatible registries and data packs.

## Commands

Root is `/veloflame`, alias `/velo`. `/bungeecord` and `/bungee` aliases are added for non-PRO builds, or when PRO controls allow them.

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `/veloflame` | Version, edition, and command list |
| `/veloflame reload` | Reload configuration |
| `/veloflame whitelist` | Usage and entry count |
| `/veloflame whitelist add <entry>` | Add a single-word entry |
| `/veloflame whitelist remove <entry>` | Remove an entry |
| `/veloflame whitelist list` / `clear` | List or clear entries |
| `/veloflame firewall` | Usage: `add`, `remove`, `list` |
| `/veloflame firewall add <ip>` | Add an IP |
| `/veloflame maintenance` | Status |
| `/veloflame maintenance on\|off [backend] [target]` | Global or per-backend toggle |

Whitelist and maintenance arguments use Velocity's single-word string argument, so entries cannot contain spaces.

The README also documents inherited upstream commands. This page does not reproduce them, because they are upstream docs rather than VeloFlame-specific behavior verified here.

## Permissions

These four nodes are checked in source:

| Node | Where enforced |
| --- | --- |
| `veloflame.reload` | `VeloFlameCommand` |
| `veloflame.whitelist` | `WhitelistSubcommand` |
| `veloflame.firewall` | `FirewallSubcommand` |
| `veloflame.maintenance` | `MaintenanceSubcommand` |

No descriptor declares these nodes, so there are **no default values**. Assign them through your permission plugin. Do not assume operator grants. Upstream `velocity.command.*` nodes appear only in the inherited README. `velocity.command.gkick` is the one code-confirmed sample.

## Troubleshooting

VeloFlame has **no troubleshooting document or section**. Only inline config comments cover failure behavior. Firewall setup failure falls back to the Java-side cache. Seamless switching carries a registry compatibility warning. Limbo testing requires removing localhost and private entries from the global whitelist. Do not treat those comments as a diagnostic guide.
